textbookText: Activity 2.4: Visit the nearby pond or lake and collect water samples containing algae. Place a small drop of water sample onto a glass slide and cover it with a coverslip. Observe the slide under the microscope. Write the morphology, cell structure etc. of algae and draw the picture on chart paper and present in class.
Kingdom Division Class Order Family Genus
: Plantae : Algae : Chlorophyceae : Conjugales : Zygnemaceae : Spirogyra

Occurrence It is one of the common green algae found as free floating masses in the still water of reservoirs, tanks, pools, lakes, ditches, and slow running streams and rivers. Due to silky long filament and slippery nature, it is also known as pond scum or water silk.

Fig: 2.4.4 (a) Spirogyra in habitat (b) Spirogyra filament under microscope (c) Spirogyra under high resolution Plant body The plant body is green, cylindrical thallus. It is thread like long unbranched filament. The filament is slimy due to presence of mucilage sheath. Each filament consists hundreds of similar cells placed end to end in a single row. The young filaments are attached to the substratum while the adult plants are free floating.

Cell structure The cells of the filament are cylindrical in form and consist of two parts, the cell wall and the protoplast. The cell wall surrounds the protoplast and is protective in function. It consists of two layers; inner layer is made up of cellulose and forms a complete envelope around the protoplast while the outer layer is made of pectin substances. The protoplast is differentiated into plasma membrane, cytoplasm, nucleus, one or more chloroplast and a central vacuole. The Biology, Grade 11 | 112
